entities.name: 13-month-old ETT choice
observations: For a 13-month-old requiring mechanical ventilation, a low-pressure cuffed oral ETT is preferred; a 3.5-mm internal diameter is the most practical initial size, with 3.0- and 4.0-mm tubes available.
Cuffed-tube formula ID = age in years/4 + 3.5 gives approximately 3.77 mm at 13 months, supporting a 3.5–4.0-mm cuffed range.
Cuff pressure should be measured and kept within local/manufacturer safety limits; tube position and ventilation must be confirmed.
Former prematurity at 30 weeks alone does not require an uncuffed tube or a different initial tube type at 13 months.

entities.name: 3.5-mm cuffed ETT
observations: Recommended initial oral endotracheal tube choice for this 13-month-old requiring mechanical ventilation, assuming no known abnormal airway anatomy.

entities.name: 4.0-mm cuffed ETT
observations: Reasonable larger backup tube if the 3.5-mm tube is too small or has excessive leak, provided passage and cuff pressure are appropriate.
